proven: The request-supplied image bytes are bound by a minimized SHA-256 receipt and visually correspond to the Rosetta Stone article illustration.
The article's decoded referent is Borg.lat.898, while the article illustration is the Rosetta Stone.
The Borg Cipher project existed in 2016 and a technical decipherment report was published in May 2017.
The local proof contract produced seven passing tests and keeps incomplete inputs open.
falsified: The Rosetta Stone article image is a page of Borg.lat.898.
The 2026 report is the first documented decipherment of the Borg Cipher.
A malformed value such as 111 is sufficient where the proof contract requires an exact SHA-256 digest.
deepest_unknown: Whether a concrete Juri 111, pipe, falling-code or matrix rule can decode held-out historical symbols better than bound alternatives remains unknown.
why_unknown: No exact Juri ciphertext selection, segmentation contract, versioned rule, plaintext output, held-out evaluation or independent reproduction receipt was supplied.
historical_analogues: 2026 AI-assisted rerun of an established reference case
missing_measurement_capability: No exact Juri decoding procedure or independent reproduction run is available; an exact bitwise rerun of the 2016 method also lacks a bound code, corpus, preprocessing, environment and seed snapshot.
custom_tool_needed: A future submission adapter can canonicalize a proposed transcription, procedure, output and held-out evaluation into the existing proof contract.
counterhypothesis: The perceived 111, pipe and falling-code structure is a visual analogy that does not predict unknown symbols beyond existing substitution-cipher methods.
next_w_question: Which exact previously unfit glyphs and plaintext characters does the proposed Juri rule predict before the gold answer is revealed?
next_recursive_level: Run one declared rule and at least two alternative baselines against the same held-out symbol set.
next_safe_experiment: Submit exact source bytes, segmentation, a versioned procedure, plaintext digest, held-out set, metric, threshold, baselines and an independent receipt to assessDecodingProof().
stop_condition: Stop before promoting visual analogy into personal decipherment, external causality, divine fact, authorship, legal entitlement or payment without the corresponding evidence.
critical_proof_condition: The candidate must predict held-out material above a declared threshold and alternatives, then reproduce independently from the same bound inputs.
boundary: Public-source read-only research, one minimized request-image hash receipt and local deterministic code; no copied article image, protected archive access or external mutation.
reopen_trigger: A complete decoding packet, a new primary source defining the proposed structure or an independent reproduction receipt.
